This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`cat-7-portfolio.md`](cat-7-portfolio.md), with the same sections, files and
numbers. The text under each R chunk is what the chunk prints.
`R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` checks that each chunk prints exactly that
text.

Larkspur Re holds five contracts on three cedents, and one windstorm can hit
all of them in the same year. This page adds the five contracts into one book,
measures the tail of the book, splits its capital back to the contracts, and
shows which contracts pay for their capital.

The story, the files and the notation are on
[the overview](cat-0-overview.qmd). The page types no number by hand: every
attachment, limit and share comes from `cat_book_contracts.csv`.

## 1. The idea

Each row of the year event loss table belongs to one simulated year, and every
contract sees the same 2,000 years. The loss of the book in a year is the sum
of the losses of the five contracts. The events carry the dependence: one event
in the catalog lands on several cedents at once. No copula or reordering is
needed.

That is the only dependence here. The script that wrote the book draws each
cedent's loss from an event independently, so the correlated part of secondary
uncertainty (page 1) is not correlated across cedents. A model that shares it
would give the book a heavier tail.

Three questions follow from the sum.

- **How bad is the bad year?** TVaR at 99% of the summed loss: the mean of the
  worst 1% of years.
- **Which contracts cause it?** The Euler split: each contract's mean loss in
  the years that make the tail of the book.
  [Price allocation](pir-price-allocation.qmd) compares other splits.
- **Does each contract pay for its capital?** A return on allocated capital,
  against the premium charged.

## 2. The book

The chunk repeats the helpers of the earlier pages (each guide runs on its own),
builds a tower for each contract on its subject loss, and wraps each result in a
`deal_run_from_tower()`. A `deal_book()` aligns the runs by year.

```{r}
library(prospicio)

# The data files, found from the repository root (CI) or from docs/guides (Quarto).
find_data <- function(name, dir = getwd()) {
  repeat {
    path <- file.path(dir, "examples", "data", name)
    if (file.exists(path)) return(path)
    parent <- dirname(dir)
    if (identical(parent, dir)) stop("examples/data/", name, " not found", call. = FALSE)
    dir <- parent
  }
}

read_text <- function(name) read.csv(find_data(name), colClasses = "character")
YELT <- read_text("cat_book_yelt.csv")
CONTRACTS <- read_text("cat_book_contracts.csv")
CEDENTS <- read_text("cat_book_cedents.csv")
N_YEARS <- 2000

# One cedent's years of losses, with times (fraction of the year) and peril labels.
cedent_events <- function(cedent, perils = "all") {
  rows <- YELT[YELT$cedent == cedent, ]
  if (perils != "all") rows <- rows[rows$peril %in% strsplit(perils, "+", fixed = TRUE)[[1]], ]
  year <- factor(as.integer(rows$year), levels = seq_len(N_YEARS))
  time <- ((as.integer(rows$day) - 1) * 24 + as.integer(rows$hour)) / 8760
  ev <- events_from_years(unname(split(as.double(rows$loss), year)),
                          times = unname(split(time, year)))
  with_labels(ev, list(peril = rows$peril[order(year)]))
}

num <- function(x, default = NULL) if (x != "") as.double(x) else default

# The contract's terms from cat_book_contracts.csv as a layer.
contract_layer <- function(c) {
  share <- num(c$share)
  if (c$kind == "occurrence_xl") {
    limit <- num(c$limit)
    return(xol_layer(c$contract, limit, num(c$attachment), share = share,
                     premium = num(c$rate_on_line) * limit * share,
                     reinstatement_rates = rep(num(c$reinstatement_rate),
                                               as.integer(c$reinstatements))))
  }
  if (c$kind == "aggregate_xl") {
    agg_limit <- num(c$aggregate_limit)
    return(xol_layer(c$contract, Inf, 0, share = share,
                     aggregate_deductible = num(c$aggregate_deductible),
                     aggregate_limit = agg_limit,
                     premium = num(c$rate_on_line) * agg_limit * share))
  }
  premium <- share * as.double(CEDENTS$cat_premium[CEDENTS$cedent == c$cedent])
  with_ceding_commission(
    xol_layer(c$contract, num(c$limit), 0, share = share,
              aggregate_limit = num(c$aggregate_limit), premium = premium),
    num(c$ceding_commission))
}

# The contract's subject loss: its cedent and perils, grouped by its hours clause.
subject <- function(c) {
  e <- cedent_events(c$cedent, c$perils)
  if (c$hours != "") hours_clause(e, as.double(c$hours)) else e
}

deals <- CONTRACTS$contract
towers <- list()
results <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(CONTRACTS))) {
  c <- CONTRACTS[i, ]
  towers[[c$contract]] <- reinsurance_tower(list(contract_layer(c)))
  results[[c$contract]] <- apply_tower(towers[[c$contract]], subject(c))
}
runs <- lapply(deals, function(d) deal_run_from_tower(d, towers[[d]], results[[d]], d))
book <- deal_book(runs)
amounts <- book_amounts(book)
cat(sprintf("%d deals, %d years\n", length(runs), as.integer(amounts@n_sims)))
cat("items:", paste(unique(amounts@keys$item), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```text
5 deals, 2000 years
items: premium, loss, ceding_commission, total_deductions, nmbf, margin
```

`book_summary()` gives the mean of every item by deal and for the book, with its
ratio to the mean premium. Premium is the yearly deposit plus the reinstatement
premium that the year's losses pay (section 3). Margin is premium less loss less
deductions (only `corran_qs` has any: its ceding commission). The data has no
expenses of Larkspur, so the margin is before them.

```{r}
#| label: result-table
library(gt)
s <- book_summary(book)
item_mean <- function(s, d, i) s$mean[s$deal == d & s$item == i]
item_ratio <- function(s, d, i) s$ratio[s$deal == d & s$item == i]
all_deals <- c(deals, "total")
result <- data.frame(
  deal = all_deals,
  premium = sapply(all_deals, item_mean, s = s, i = "premium"),
  loss = sapply(all_deals, item_mean, s = s, i = "loss"),
  deduct = sapply(all_deals, item_mean, s = s, i = "total_deductions") + 0,
  margin = sapply(all_deals, item_mean, s = s, i = "margin"),
  LR = sapply(all_deals, item_ratio, s = s, i = "loss")
)
gt(result, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("Mean annual result by deal", "Premium units; LR = loss / premium") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(premium, loss, deduct, margin, LR), decimals = 3)
```

```text
             premium   loss  deduct  margin     LR
alder_cat_1    1.921  0.823   0.000   1.098  0.428
alder_cat_2    1.020  0.416   0.000   0.604  0.408
bracken_cat    1.846  0.685   0.000   1.161  0.371
bracken_agg    0.450  0.162   0.000   0.288  0.360
corran_qs      3.000  1.202   0.750   1.048  0.401
total          8.237  3.289   0.750   4.198  0.399
```

## 3. Reinstatement premium in the book

`deal_run_from_tower()` adds the reinstatement premium of each year to the
deposit premium of the layer. The tower computes it for the two Alder layers
and `bracken_cat`, pro rata as to amount, so `alder_cat_1` earns 1.8 in a quiet
year and more in a year that reaches the layer.
`reinstatement_premium = FALSE` keeps the deposit alone. The losses and the
capital below do not change; the premium and the margin do.

```{r}
premium <- marginal(amounts, c("premium", "alder_cat_1"))@draws
cat(sprintf("alder_cat_1 book premium: min %.3f, max %.3f\n", min(premium), max(premium)))
deposit <- deal_book(lapply(deals, function(d) {
  deal_run_from_tower(d, towers[[d]], results[[d]], d, reinstatement_premium = FALSE)
}))
s_dep <- book_summary(deposit)
```

```text
alder_cat_1 book premium: min 1.800, max 3.600
```

```{r}
#| label: reinstatement-table
reinstatement <- data.frame(
  deal = deals,
  premium = sapply(deals, item_mean, s = s, i = "premium"),
  deposit = sapply(deals, item_mean, s = s_dep, i = "premium")
)
reinstatement$reinstatement <- reinstatement$premium - reinstatement$deposit
gt(reinstatement, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("Reinstatement premium by deal", "Mean per year, premium units") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(premium, deposit), decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_number(columns = reinstatement, decimals = 4)
```

```text
             premium  deposit  reinstatement
alder_cat_1    1.921    1.800         0.1207
alder_cat_2    1.020    1.000         0.0203
bracken_cat    1.846    1.750         0.0959
bracken_agg    0.450    0.450         0.0000
corran_qs      3.000    3.000         0.0000
```

## 4. The book's tail

`book_distribution(book, "loss", ...)` gives three views of each deal at once.

- `total`: the statistics of the book.
- `contribution`: the mean loss of the deal in the years that make the
  statistic of the book. For TVaR this is the Euler split, and the
  contributions add up to the TVaR of the book.
- `marginal`: the statistic of the book less the same statistic of the book
  without that deal. It answers "what would we save by not writing this?".

`capital_allocation()` gives the stand-alone TVaR of each deal, the first
column of the table.

```{r}
dist <- book_distribution(book, "loss", 99, tvar_levels = 99)
loss <- select_components(select_components(amounts, "item", "loss"), "deal", deals)
alloc <- capital_allocation(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99))
cat(sprintf("book: mean %.3f, VaR 99 %.3f, TVaR 99 %.3f\n", dist$total[["Mean"]],
            dist$total[["Percentile 99"]], dist$total[["TVaR 99"]]))
cat(sprintf("sum of contributions %.3f\n", sum(dist$contribution["TVaR 99", deals])))
```

```text
book: mean 3.289, VaR 99 46.505, TVaR 99 55.096
sum of contributions 55.096
```

```{r}
#| label: tail-table
tail_tvar <- data.frame(
  deal = deals,
  alone = alloc$by_component$standalone,
  contrib = unname(dist$contribution["TVaR 99", deals]),
  marginal = unname(dist$marginal["TVaR 99", deals])
)
gt(tail_tvar, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("TVaR 99 of the loss by deal", "Premium units") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(alone, contrib, marginal), decimals = 3)
```

```text
              alone  contrib  marginal
alder_cat_1  13.843   13.195    12.728
alder_cat_2  20.998   19.026    14.560
bracken_cat  14.136    9.397     8.840
bracken_agg   7.500    0.262     0.193
corran_qs    16.363   13.216    12.609
```

```{r}
#| label: tail-figure
library(ggplot2, exclude = "layer")   # keeps prospicio's layer()
tail_views <- rbind(
  data.frame(deal = deals, view = "alone", tvar = alloc$by_component$standalone),
  data.frame(deal = deals, view = "contribution (Euler)", tvar = dist$contribution["TVaR 99", deals]),
  data.frame(deal = deals, view = "marginal", tvar = dist$marginal["TVaR 99", deals])
)
tail_views$deal <- factor(tail_views$deal, levels = deals)
tail_views$view <- factor(tail_views$view, levels = c("alone", "contribution (Euler)", "marginal"))
ggplot(tail_views, aes(deal, tvar, fill = view)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("alone" = "grey75", "contribution (Euler)" = scales::hue_pal()(2)[1],
                               "marginal" = scales::hue_pal()(2)[2])) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "TVaR 99 of the loss (premium units)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Tail of the book: alone, in the book, and removed from it") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

By deal:

- `alder_cat_2`, the high Alder layer, has the largest TVaR alone and keeps most
  of it in the book: the years that exhaust it are the big coastal windstorms
  that drive the whole book.
- `bracken_agg` looks risky alone: in its worst 1% of years it pays its whole
  aggregate limit. Those are mostly years of one large flood or storm outbreak
  on the plains (page 3, section 5), not the worst of the book, so it adds
  little to the tail of the book.
- Contributions add up to the TVaR of the book. Marginals do not: removing a deal
  changes the worst years.

## 5. A trap: the total row

`book_amounts()` holds every item for each deal *and* a `"total"` deal. A
selection on the item alone keeps that total, so `capital_allocation()` adds it
to the deals as a sixth contract and the TVaR of the book doubles.

```{r}
wrong <- capital_allocation(select_components(amounts, "item", "loss"), distortion("tvar", 0.99))
right <- capital_allocation(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99))
cat(sprintf("item only: total %.3f, components %d\n", wrong$total, nrow(wrong$by_component)))
cat(sprintf("item and deals: total %.3f, components %d\n", right$total,
            nrow(right$by_component)))
```

```text
item only: total 110.192, components 6
item and deals: total 55.096, components 5
```

Select the deals by name, `select_components(..., "deal", deals)`, every time.

## 6. Capital and diversification

`capital_allocation(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99))` allocates the TVaR of the
book by Euler, so the allocated amounts are the contributions above.
Diversification is the sum of the stand-alone TVaRs less the TVaR of the book:

```
diversification = sum over deals i of TVaR(X_i) - TVaR(X_1 + ... + X_5)
```

TVaR is subadditive, so this is never negative.

```{r}
#| label: diversification-table
bc <- alloc$by_component
divers <- data.frame(
  deal = deals,
  alone = bc$standalone,
  allocated = bc$allocated,
  saved = bc$diversification
)
gt(divers, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("Capital by deal: alone and in the book",
             "TVaR 99, premium units; saved = alone - allocated") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(alone, allocated, saved), decimals = 3)
```

```text
              alone  allocated  saved
alder_cat_1  13.843     13.195  0.648
alder_cat_2  20.998     19.026  1.973
bracken_cat  14.136      9.397  4.738
bracken_agg   7.500      0.262  7.238
corran_qs    16.363     13.216  3.147
```

```{r}
cat(sprintf("sum alone %.3f, book %.3f, benefit %.3f\n", sum(bc$standalone), alloc$total,
            alloc$diversification_benefit))
```

```text
sum alone 72.840, book 55.096, benefit 17.744
```

## 7. The book priced on its capital

`price_portfolio()` prices the book as page 6, section 2 prices one contract:
`P = (EL + r A) / (1 + r)`, with the assets `A` now the TVaR of the book. It
splits that premium to the deals by the same Euler weights
([portfolio pricing](pir-portfolio-pricing.qmd) has the theory), and prices each
deal alone. Compare these prices with what Larkspur keeps: the premium
charged, plus the expected reinstatement premium of section 3, less the
deductions (the ceding commission of Corran).

```{r}
pp <- price_portfolio(loss, distortion("tvar", 0.99), cost_of_capital = 0.10)
cat(sprintf("book: EL %.3f, premium %.3f, capital %.3f\n", pp$total$expected_loss,
            pp$total$premium, pp$total$capital))
cat(sprintf("premium saved by diversification %.3f\n", pp$diversification))
kept <- function(d) item_mean(s, d, "premium") - item_mean(s, d, "total_deductions")
```

```text
book: EL 3.289, premium 7.998, capital 47.097
premium saved by diversification 1.613
```

```{r}
#| label: prices-table
prices <- data.frame(
  deal = c(deals, "book"),
  charged = sapply(all_deals, item_mean, s = s_dep, i = "premium"),
  kept = sapply(all_deals, kept),
  in_book = c(pp$by_component$premium, pp$total$premium),
  alone = c(pp$by_component$standalone_premium, NA)
)
gt(prices, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("Premium by deal: charged, kept and needed",
             "Premium units; needed = cost of capital 10% on TVaR 99 capital") |>
  tab_spanner("needed", columns = c(in_book, alone)) |>
  cols_label(in_book = "in book") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(charged, kept, in_book, alone), decimals = 3) |>
  sub_missing(columns = alone, missing_text = "")
```

```text
             charged   kept  in book  alone
alder_cat_1    1.800  1.921    1.948  2.007
alder_cat_2    1.000  1.020    2.108  2.287
bracken_cat    1.750  1.846    1.477  1.908
bracken_agg    0.450  0.450    0.171  0.829
corran_qs      3.000  2.250    2.295  2.581
book           8.000  7.487    7.998
```

Alone, `alder_cat_1` needs the 2.007 of page 6. In the book it needs 1.948.
The book charges 8.000 against the 7.998 that a 10% return on TVaR capital
needs, but keeps 7.487 after the reinstatement premium comes in and the ceding
commission of Corran goes out. So the book falls short of the target (section 9:
a 9.0% return). Both Alder layers keep less than their share, `alder_cat_2`
about half of it. The Bracken contracts keep more. The quota share of Corran
keeps 2.250 of 3.000, a little under its 2.295.

## 8. The marginal price of a new contract

The allocated price shares the price of the book among the deals already
written. A new contract asks what it must charge so that the return of the book
does not fall. Its extra assets `dA` are its marginal TVaR (the book with it
less the book without it), and `EL` is its expected loss:

```
P = EL + r * (dA - P),   so   P = (EL + r * dA) / (1 + r)
```

Below, each deal in turn is the last one written. The chunk computes the price
from `marginal` (#588).

```{r}
#| label: marginal-table
r <- 0.10
marg <- data.frame(
  deal = deals,
  EL = unname(dist$marginal["Mean", deals]),
  dA = unname(dist$marginal["TVaR 99", deals])
)
marg$marginal_P <- (marg$EL + r * marg$dA) / (1 + r)
marg$charged <- sapply(deals, item_mean, s = s_dep, i = "premium")
gt(marg, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("Marginal price of each deal as the last one written",
             "Premium units; P = (EL + r dA) / (1 + r), r = 10%") |>
  cols_label(marginal_P = "marginal P") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(EL, dA, marginal_P, charged), decimals = 3)
```

```text
                EL      dA  marginal P  charged
alder_cat_1  0.823  12.728       1.905    1.800
alder_cat_2  0.416  14.560       1.702    1.000
bracken_cat  0.685   8.840       1.426    1.750
bracken_agg  0.162   0.193       0.165    0.450
corran_qs    1.202  12.609       2.239    3.000
```

```{r}
#| label: marginal-figure
marginal_p <- (dist$marginal["Mean", deals] + r * dist$marginal["TVaR 99", deals]) / (1 + r)
compare <- rbind(
  data.frame(deal = deals, price = "charged", premium = sapply(deals, function(d) item_mean(s_dep, d, "premium"))),
  data.frame(deal = deals, price = "marginal price", premium = marginal_p)
)
compare$deal <- factor(compare$deal, levels = deals)
compare$price <- factor(compare$price, levels = c("charged", "marginal price"))
ggplot(compare, aes(deal, premium, fill = price)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("charged" = "grey75", "marginal price" = scales::hue_pal()(1))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "premium (premium units)", fill = NULL,
       title = "Charged premium against the marginal price of each deal") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Every marginal price is below the allocated price, because a deal's marginal
TVaR is at most its Euler contribution (TVaR is subadditive). Price the next
contract on its marginal, and the TVaR return holds. Price every contract on
its marginal, and the book falls short.

## 9. A return on allocated capital

A risk-adjusted return on capital (RAROC) sets the margin of each deal against
its allocated capital: the allocated assets less the premium of the deal. The
margin includes the reinstatement premium of section 3, and there is no expense
line, so the return is before the costs of Larkspur.

```{r}
#| label: returns-table
returns <- data.frame(
  deal = c(deals, "book"),
  margin = sapply(c(deals, "total"), function(d) item_mean(s, d, "margin")),
  capital = c(bc$allocated - sapply(deals, function(d) item_mean(s, d, "premium")),
              alloc$total - item_mean(s, "total", "premium"))
)
returns$return <- ifelse(returns$capital > 0, returns$margin / returns$capital, NA_real_)
gt(returns, rowname_col = "deal") |>
  tab_header("Return on allocated capital", "Premium units; return = margin / capital") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(margin, capital), decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = return, decimals = 1) |>
  sub_missing(columns = return, missing_text = "none")
```

```text
             margin  capital  return
alder_cat_1   1.098   11.274    9.7%
alder_cat_2   0.604   18.005    3.4%
bracken_cat   1.161    7.552   15.4%
bracken_agg   0.288   -0.188    none
corran_qs     1.048   10.216   10.3%
book          4.198   46.859    9.0%
```

Against a 10% target, `alder_cat_2` is the weak contract: it uses over a third
of the capital of the book and returns a few percent. `bracken_agg` has no
return: its premium exceeds the assets allocated to it, so it needs no
shareholder capital here, and a ratio over negative capital has no meaning.

## 10. Reproducibility

The VaR of the book is the default inverted-cdf quantile; page 2, section 2
compares the other conventions. Every number on this page follows from four
committed files and one seed.

- `examples/data/make_cat_book.py` writes the files with a fixed seed. A test
  checks that the committed files are what the script writes.
- No step draws a random number: the book adds the same 2,000 years for every
  contract.
- `read_ylt()` stamps the event set with a hash of the file that it read, so you
  can trace a result to its input. The rebuild by `cedent_events()` drops that
  hash, so record it from `read_ylt()` once.

```{r}
ylt <- read_ylt(find_data("cat_book_yelt.csv"), year = "year", loss = "loss", slot = "slot",
                labels = c("peril", "region", "cedent"))
cat(strsplit(ylt@input_hash, ":", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1], ylt@n_sims, "\n")
```

```text
blake3 2000
```

The page does not print the hash: it depends on the bytes of the file, and a
checkout that changes line endings to CRLF gives a different hash.
